Subject: Your first order with us — a few things worth knowing
CTA: Read our gear buying guides -> https://www.northbaysupply.com/buying-guides
Body: Hey,

Glad you've been spending time with us lately. Before you make your first purchase, we want to give you something more useful than a discount code: a straight read on how to shop for outdoor gear without second-guessing yourself later.

**Match the gear to the trip, not the other way around.**
The most common mistake is buying for the trip you imagine rather than the one you're actually taking. Before you add anything to your cart, write down three things: where you're going, how long you'll be out, and what the conditions will realistically be. Weight, capacity, and weather ratings only matter in relation to those answers.

**Pay attention to the numbers.**
Adjectives like 'lightweight' or 'packable' mean different things to different brands. Look at the actual grams, liters, and ratings — those are comparable. A sleeping bag rated to 20°F performs differently than one rated to 32°F, and that gap matters at 2 a.m.

**Know what gear isn't built for.**
Every piece of equipment has a designed-for range. A three-season tent is not a winter tent. A trail-running shoe is not a mountaineering boot. We'll always tell you what something is not meant to handle — that's not a knock on the product, it's just honest.

**Buy for the trip you're taking this season.**
It's tempting to gear up for everything at once. Instead, identify the one or two gaps that would actually affect your next trip and start there. You'll make better choices, and you won't end up with a closet full of gear that doesn't fit how you actually move.

When you're ready to browse, our buying guides walk you through specs category by category — no filler, just the information you need to make a confident call.

See you on the trail.

— The Northbay Supply Team
